newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr clings to bid tone, but must act fast.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr clings to bid tone, but must act fast.

text.p: The dollar sat through a quiet Monday session but could face near-term slippage if it fails to take out last week's three-year highs near 1.7270 marks, technical analysts said.
With little resistance seen between those highs and 1.74 marks, the dollar could enjoy rapid gains if it can reignite last week's stalled rally, chartists said.

"There really isn't that much momentum right now, but the dollar does look bid. There isn't that much resistance up (above 1.7270). It's sort of virgin territory," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
Late in the session, the greenback pressed higher to touch 1.73 marks, its highest point since it traded at 1.7405 during the week of February 27, 1994.
That move could help extend the current dollar/mark rally and open up the possibility of a move to 1.74, chartists said.
"We don't have any evidence yet that a top is in place because we've been holding so close to last week's highs," said Joseph Klettner, foreign exchange technician at Chase Securities Inc.
Klettner sees the dollar near the end of a fifth wave of a bull phase, which began after a March 31 low at 1.6610 marks.
Dollar/yen sat little changed during the late dollar/mark rally, but analysts said dollar/yen could easily follow up with gains of its own later in the week.
"Dollar/yen has been lagging dollar/mark a bit, but there as well, the trend is for a stronger dollar," said Autotte.
The dollar faces resistance at last week's 56-month high of 127.19, but in the meantime failed to beat congestion resistance at 126.60, chartists noted.
"Dollar/yen looks like its only completed four waves (of a five-step Elliott Wave pattern)," Klettner said. "That opens up the possibility of a rally to a marginal new high."
Like dollar/yen, mark/yen appears ready for an upside thrust, but has recently disappointed bulls with its failure to rally.
With good support at 73.05 and resistance at 73.60, mark/yen consolidated on Monday, but could challenge the 74 area and test resistance at 74.40-50 in the near term, Autotte said.
"We saw a nice triangle forming late last week and I thought mark/yen would explode to the topside, but we're still moving within the triangle on the daily charts.
